title: Plug Your Volt: Protecting Intel Processors against Dynamic Voltage Frequency Scaling based Fault Attacks
problem: DVFS-based fault attacks exploit independent frequency-voltage control on Intel processors to induce computational faults. Existing countermeasures prevent benign processes from using DVFS and rely on less practical threat models than real-world Intel SGX deployments.
motivation: Defending modern Intel processors against practical DVFS fault attacks while preserving power management capabilities for legitimate workloads.
method: The work identifies independent frequency-voltage control as the root cause of DVFS faults and partitions frequency-voltage tuples into safe and unsafe states using switching circuit theory to predict timing violations. The countermeasure enforces only safe frequency-voltage combinations and can be deployed via microcode updates or model-specific registers.
key_novelty: Using switching circuit theory to formally partition frequency-voltage combinations into provably safe and unsafe states, enabling a deployable countermeasure without restricting benign DVFS usage.
contributions: Established that independent frequency-voltage control is the fundamental cause of DVFS fault attacks
Developed a switching-circuit-theory-based partition method to classify safe and unsafe frequency-voltage tuples
Demonstrated complete DVFS fault prevention on three Intel generations (Sky Lake, Kaby Lake R, Comet Lake)
Achieved only 0.28% performance overhead on SPEC2017 with flexible microcode and MSR-based deployment
primary_theme: DVFS fault attack mitigation via frequency-voltage constraint enforcement
